rationale: Jesus names the earlier event Himself: "Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand, and how many basketfuls you gathered?" (16:9, BSB), recalling "We have here only five loaves of bread and two fish" (14:17) and "twelve basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over" (14:20). Naming the earlier event is why the type is explicit_reference and the label explicit, as with conn-matt12-nineveh-jonah3, where Jesus names Nineveh and Jonah's preaching. The Greek confirms the link at the level of the word: 16:9 and 14:20 both use kophinos for the baskets in all nine editions Bible Hub lists, while 16:10 and 15:37 both use spyris for the four thousand (spelled sphyris in Westcott-Hort). In this app's BSB both words are rendered "basketfuls," so the distinction is visible only in Greek. Ellicott on 16:9-10 notes that the distinction "is ... strictly observed here." What the distinction means is disputed: the Pulpit Commentary takes kophinoi as small baskets and spyrides as large panniers, and Meyer holds that the difference is not size but that kophinos is general while spyris is a food basket. The companion reference in 16:10 to the four thousand (15:34-37) belongs with this curriculum's lesson on the feeding of the four thousand (Matthew 15) and is not authored here.
